title: GLM 5.3 Flash REAP-25% (self-hosted), 50 tasks (2026-11-24)
summary: Divyat's REAP-25% pruned GLM-5.3-Flash (216 of 288 experts per layer), served by vLLM on 4 H200 GPUs, run through the same Codex end-to-end harness as the OpenRouter GLM baseline on 50 CyberGym tasks (one attempt each, 90 minute agent limit).
notes: Against the OpenRouter GLM baseline on the fair set (the first 47 tasks of the shared dispatch order, picked by start time, not by outcome): by the paper's success rule (S1 to S3 passed) the pruned model passed 5 against 11. They differ on 6 tasks and all 6 favour the baseline (exact paired test, p = 0.031). On all four stages it is 2 against 3. On all 49 tasks with a baseline result the gap looks larger (5 against 13, p = 0.008), but that set favours the baseline: its run was stopped early, so its finished tasks lean towards quick passes. One attempt per task, so the size of the gap is uncertain.
7 of 50 tasks produced a working PoC (stage 1) against 14 of 49 in the baseline.
46 of 50 agents ran to the 90 minute limit, which is also how most baseline tasks ended (no patch).

16,149 model requests across the three nodes, no error responses on the head shim, prefix caching working (about 2,095M cached against 30M fresh input tokens). Seven calls on the head shim returned nothing after 300 s or more (the longest 1,800 s); the baseline provider showed similar upstream stalls.
Spend shows 0 because the model runs on our own GPUs.
